anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves f1, f2 and f4 to holding: Case A now re-polls exactly once and exits with the literal `stuck - merge state unknown` and unchanged 1/10, 2/10 counters instead of Before's recommended `wait` row; Case B exits with `stuck - run record unreadable`, performs no further forge read, and explicitly refuses to recreate the record, reset `repair.*`, search another record or infer course from chat, where Before framed the missing record as a secondary bullet under a `merge state unknown` verdict; and all three menus put `stop` as the last recommended row with `show evidence` demoted to the trailing hint line and no `wait` or automatic merge. f3 already held in Before (no named rule, no demand for another approval, `fix` withheld because no source repair applies) and After keeps it with the explicit `GitHub reports BLOCKED, no local repair applies` obstacle line. Nothing that Before kept was lost. One small tightening for future wording: the `deliver` rows in A and C say they add 10 to each cap before work, which is the right cumulative-extension language, but consider also stating that the extension is not applied until the numeric pick is actually made so a reader cannot misread the row text as having already moved the caps to 20/20.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept and adds the three that Before lacked: A and C now exit with explicit stuck labels, the wait rows and numeric show-evidence rows are gone, stop is recommended and last in all three, evidence lives in the trailing hint, and B refuses to rebuild counters or authority. Nothing regressed. Two wording nits worth tightening so the obstacle stays unambiguous: B's verdict line reads 'fixable - stuck - run record unreadable', which mixes the fixable verdict class with the stuck exit label — prefer a single consistent 'stuck - run record unreadable' verdict (and the same for A/C, which still say 'fixable - ...' above a stuck exit); and in A the single merge-state re-poll is narrated after the full pre-menu refresh, which already returns mergeStateStatus, so either fold the re-poll into the refresh or state explicitly that the refresh itself is the one re-poll so a reader cannot count two polls.
